newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bank sector faces new round of staff cuts.
newsitem.headline: Danish bank sector faces new round of staff cuts.

text.p: Major staff cuts are expected in Denmark's bank sector in 1997 and 1998, according to estimates Reuters received from leading banks on Tuesday.
Unidanmark, Denmark's second biggest bank, said it expected staff to fall by around 500 during 1997, mainly through natural redundancy.

"In our budget for 1997, we are calculating with a net reduction in staff of around 500, but unlike other big banks, most of the cuts will take place through natural wastage," director Preben Kendal told Reuters.
Unidanmark had around 10,000 staff in total at the turn of the year, after shedding some 500 jobs during 1996.

Earlier this month, Den Danske Bank, the country's biggest, announced plans to reduce staff by the 500 during the year, followed by the third biggest, BG Bank, which said on Monday it planned some 300 redundancies in 1997.

According to banking organisation estimates, the total number of employees in Denmark's bank sector will fall by some 2,500 to around 41,800 this year, with a further 2,300 expected to face dismissal in 1998.
